concept.name: Exit criterion
concept.definition: The predefined rules governing when and how a position is closed - profit targets, stop or invalidation exits, time stops, and trailing logic. Exit criteria are decided at entry so that exits respond to information and structure rather than to fear or greed in real time.
concept.intuition: Anyone can get into a trade; the exit is where the P&L is actually written, so it cannot be improvised mid-emotion.
concept.mechanics: Typically combines an invalidation exit (stop), one or more profit-taking rules (fixed target, measured move, trailing stop), and optionally a time stop; exchange order types (stop, stop-limit, trailing stop) implement them mechanically. Together with entry and size, exit rules determine the trade's R-multiple distribution.
concept.failure_modes: Exits improvised under stress systematically become 'sell winners early, hold losers' - the disposition effect. Targets placed at widely watched round numbers invite slippage, and stops at obvious levels invite stop-runs.
concept.misconceptions: Letting winners run without any exit rule is not a strategy - trailing or target logic is still required. Exiting at the planned stop is not a failure of the trade; it is the design working.
concept.example: Plan: stop at 47.8, scale out half at +2R, trail the remainder below each higher low; when price tags the second target, the rest exits on the first close below the prior swing low.
